content.text:
I've implemented the "Fightlytics Landing v2" design from Claude Design into `landing/`:

- `landing/index.html` — replaces the "Hello World" placeholder with the real page shell (fonts, favicon, React/Babel CDN scripts)
- `landing/app/logo.jsx`, `landing/app/mockup.jsx`, `landing/app/v2.jsx` — the glove logo, analysis-player mockup, and the scroll-driven product story (hero → statement → stats reel → capability gallery → Studio/Broadcast comparison → final CTA)
- `landing/app/styles.css`, `landing/app/sections.css`, `landing/app/v2.css` — the full styling stack these components depend on
- Removed the now-unused placeholder `landing/style.css`

I verified all files serve correctly over a local HTTP server (200s on the page, JSX, and CSS). Note: I don't have a browser/screenshot tool in this environment, so I could not visually render it — only confirmed the files are byte-for-byte faithful to the Claude Design source and serve without 404s. I'd recommend opening `landing/index.html` in a browser yourself to sanity-check the scroll animations before shipping.

Two things worth flagging:
- The nav/footer/"Broadcast" card link to `Fightlytics Broadcast.html`, which wasn't part of this task's scope — that link will 404 locally until that page is implemented too.
- The "Studio" CTA points to `https://app.fightlytics.com` as authored in the design.

when i open index.html I get the following error: Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'file:///Users/filip.culig/Developer/fight-ai/landing/app/logo.jsx' from origin 'null' has been blocked by CORS policy: Cross origin requests are only supported for protocol schemes: brave, chrome, chrome-experimental-site-token-provider, chrome-extension, chrome-untrusted, data, http, https, isolated-app.

That's expected with `file://` — Babel's `<script type="text/babel" src="...">` does an XHR fetch to load the JSX, which browsers block under the `file:` origin. It needs to be served over `http://` instead. This isn't a bug in the page, just a limitation of opening it directly by double-clicking.

Run a local server from the `landing/` directory and open it via `http://localhost`:

input.description: Start a local server for the landing page and confirm it responds

content.text:
A local server is running. Open **http://localhost:8123/** in your browser (not the `file://` path) and the CORS error should be gone.

When you're done previewing, let me know and I'll stop the server — or run `pkill -f "http.server 8123"` yourself.
